La descomposición la descubrieron casi a: The decomposition was discovered almost at the same time by Eugenio Beltrami, in 1873, and Camille Jordan, in 1874. The result that truncating it gives the best approximation is due to Carl Eckart and Gale Young, two quantitative psychologists, in 1936. But its great age came with computers: in 1965 Gene Golub and William Kahan gave a stable algorithm for computing it, and in the Netflix contest from 2006 to 2009, which offered a million dollars for improving film recommendations, the winning techniques were based on factorising the huge matrix of user ratings, with ideas directly related to this one.
La descomposición se puede escribir tamb: The decomposition can also be written as a sum of very simple matrices, each formed by a single product of a column vector by a row vector. And since the singular values are ordered from largest to smallest, the first terms contain what is most important in the matrix.

Los [[av-lineal|autovalores]] tienen un: [[av-lineal|Eigenvalues]] have a problem: they only exist for square matrices, and not all of those have real ones or enough eigenvectors. There is a decomposition that never fails, that exists for any matrix, square or not, and that says something very visual: every linear transformation is a rotation, followed by a stretching in perpendicular directions, followed by another rotation. It is called the singular value decomposition, and it is probably the result in linear algebra with the most applications.
